noah: putting this here in case anyone has seen it before — our onboarding sample (TS + ESM) works locally but Cloudflare worker build crashes with `TypeError: Redwood_default is not a function`.

ivy: what import style? default or named?

noah: `import Redwood from 'redwood-inference'` then `const c = Redwood<{session: string}>({ apiKey: RW_KEY })`. TS emits without errors.

sam: two likely problems: runtime export path (exports map picking cjs) or TS overloads collapsing generics. Any chance SDK publishes default overloads?

noah: yes, SDK types have two defaults: generic one and a non-generic overload. Editor shows client typed as `Client<any>` sometimes.

type-bot: quick tip: overloads where one has a generic default and another omits generic can confuse inference. TS may pick non-generic overload and caller generics are lost.

ivy: also check your tsconfig: if `esModuleInterop` is false and bundler rewrites imports to `require`, you'll hit the default export mismatch. Worker builder uses esbuild — older versions treat `exports` differently.

noah: the worker log is: `ci-cd: deploy failed: Error: TypeError: Redwood_default is not a function at worker.js:18`

sam: immediate unblocks: 1) change to named import if SDK provides it: `import { createClient } from 'redwood-inference'` and call `createClient<{...}>(...)`. 2) set `esModuleInterop: true` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: true` and `moduleResolution: "bundler"` in app tsconfig. 3) pin cloud builder (esbuild) >= 0.17.

noah: I tried `import * as Redwood` and then `Redwood.default(...)` — ugly but consistent in node; worker bundler still failed. Dynamic `await import()` worked locally but not in worker pipeline.

ivy: SDK fix suggestions: - stop publishing ambiguous default overloads; use a single exported factory with a generic parameter (preserves inference). - publish explicit ./edge subpath in package.json exports and ship per-entry .d.ts files so TS resolution matches runtime. - add a small CI matrix testing sample apps across (esModuleInterop on/off) x (ESM/CJS) x (vite/esbuild/webpack) x (node/edge).

sam: also watch for `import type` leaking into runtime if the TS pipeline isn't stripping types before esbuild. That can remove needed imports or change tree-shaking behavior.

noah: for now I switched sample to `import { createClient as Redwood }` and updated tsconfig to enable `esModuleInterop` + `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` and worker deploy succeeded. Going to open an SDK issue with repro and logs.

ivy: thanks — ping when you link the issue, we'll add it to the DX backlog and schedule the export/typing cleanup. :+1:

ci-cd: build: succeeded on next attempt after config change.
